title: Prove What Your Agent Did
content:
Most agent governance stops at “here are our logs.” That satisfies your own team. It does not satisfy a customer, a partner, or a regulator. They want evidence they can check themselves, with tools they can read.

That’s what makes this session an open source story. Imran Siddique, Chief Product Officer at OPAQUE Systems, created the Agent Governance Toolkit, an MIT-licensed policy and sandboxing layer for AI agents that Microsoft now maintains on GitHub. He also founded agentrust-io, the open home of the TRACE attestation spec, cMCP, and the Agent Manifest. Steven Mih, Founder and CEO of Action State, runs a free public witness service that any agent log can use.

Together they’ll show the TRACE Registry: a public, append-only record of agent evidence with signed checkpoints and an open source verifier. On September 7, the registry sent a 287-byte checkpoint to an independent witness and got back a receipt that verifies from published bytes, with no network calls to either company.

They’ll run that verification live, walk through what the receipt proves and what it doesn’t, and take your questions. Everything they show, you can clone and run yourself.

title: 200+ Attend State of Hiring & AI Meetup!
content:
Attendance was well over 200 and the vibe was positive and electric. Attendees were engaged and attentive as the topic was clearly one of great interest.

Taylor Desseyn of Randstad Digital powered by torc.dev delivered a very good 15-minute overview presentation looking at the current state of Hiring, and that was followed by a fantastic panel discussion featuring Anya Derbakova of AWS, Daikerra Sweat of Dell Technologies, and Bobby McNeil Jr. of Enact. Topics such as interviewing best practices, how to differentiate yourself in a crowded field, the future of programming jobs, candidate filtering using AI tooling, and many more were discussed at length.

title: May 5 Meetup Summary – 100 Attend at Wake Tech RTP
content:
Dr. Lisa Bradley, a distinguished cybersecurity expert and visionary leader currently serving as Senior Director of Product & Application Security at Dell Technologies, was the speaker and she did an amazing job.

The topic was an important one – What Enterprises Look for in OSS Under the EU Cyber Resilience Act — and How Maintainers Can Deliver It. The subtitle was Turning EU Cyber Resilience Act requirements into actionable guidance for open-source maintainers.

The topic was important because many companies in the RTP and surrounding areas, and in the ATO community, offer software products that no longer stay within the U.S. market, especially in the open source ecosystem. And because the EU Cyber Resilience Act makes cybersecurity a legal requirement, the penalty for non-compliance can be severe.

The audience was engaged throughout and an extensive Q&A session followed Dr. Bradley’s presentation.

Dr. Bradley’s slides can be found here.

The next ATO meetup is scheduled for Wednesday evening, June 24 at Cisco’s RTP campus, building #10. It’s FREE to attend but an RSVP is required. Details and an RSVP link can be found here.

Questions? Contact us at info@allthingsopen.org.

title: 2026 All Things AI Summary
content:
This was year two (2) of the conference and needless to say, it exceeded expectations.

All Monday workshop sessions “sold out”, and Tuesday’s traditional conference day sessions were overflowing with attendees (standing room only) from morning keynotes until the final end-of-day keynote at 5:30 pm ET.

Dates for 2027 have already been announced – March 22 & 23, so be sure to plan ahead and save them now!

Check out the 2027 website to see testimonials from 2026, sign up for the mailing list, and generally see what you missed.
